Prevention: Before planting, check if resistant varieties are available locally.
Plant early, as soon as weather conditions allow; this will minimize yield and grain quality losses as the crop will have matured before maximum disease development.
Rotate with non-host crops such as sorghum and legumes.
During crop growth, remove volunteer plants and weeds - grasses in particular; do not plant near eggplant or its weed relatives, e.g.
After harvest, collect and bury crop remains.
Monitoring: Small green to yellow, slightly raised spots that develop over the leaf surface, with more on the topside than the underside.
The spots growing larger, up to 2 mm, and rising further from the surface of the leaf, developing into reddish-orange pustules, round to elliptical, with yellow halos.
Masses of spores (urediniospores) that form in the pustules and spread the rust within and between crops.
Later, as the pustules age they become darker as another spore type (teliospores) appears; the leaves start to die from the tips towards the base.
The teliospores have thick walls and this helps them survive in the soil.
Spots on the stems, indicating that the infection is severe.
The disease is favoured by cool nights (15-20°C) and warm days (25-34°C) as this promotes abundant dew on the foliage, thus the development of the disease.
